Most of the excess 99215s fall on 0- and 1-condition patients, and this provider's 99215 share exceeds the all-provider rate in every complexity band. The sampled low-complexity 99215s include routine presentations such as upper respiratory infection (C0161679, C0161941, C0163089), follow-up-only Z09 visits (C0161925, C0162017, C0163147) and rash (C0162395). That is a pattern consistent with upcoding, while the sampled high-complexity 99215s (e.g., C0162336, C0163119) look plausibly supported. Documentation cannot settle the question: only one 99215 was reviewed (C0162692, documented high MDM at 48 minutes), and the single data-reviewed note without a lab line is weak evidence at most. The modest peer z-score also suggests the raw share alone is not extreme, so the risk-adjusted signal carries the case. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed, starting with the URI and Z09 visits, to check whether documented MDM and time support the billed level."}
